lines.speaker: N
lines.text: A basketball hits you in the face.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: And then... you see it coming.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: You see Jake throw it. You see it fly. You see it hit you. One full second after it already did.

lines.speaker: MIA
lines.text: Did you just... not see that?

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: Your nose is bleeding. And your eyes are still catching up.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: Because starting today... your life has lag.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: And every single day, the lag doubles.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: Here's the rule. Everything you see, hear and feel reaches you late. Your body still lives in the present. But your senses are stuck in the past.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: Day one: one second. Day two: two. Day three: four. And it never, ever stops.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: And the weird part? You were already lagging.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: Your brain needs about a tenth of a second to process what your eyes see. So every human alive is living slightly in the past. You just got... a lot worse at it.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: Day one. One second doesn't sound like much.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: Until you try to high-five someone.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: You laugh at jokes a second after everyone else. You answer questions that were already answered.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: Mia, your little sister, figures it out in about five minutes.

lines.speaker: MIA
lines.text: Watch this. Hey! Catch!

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: You do not catch.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: Soup? Messy. Stairs? Dangerous. Video games? Impossible. Your ping is now a thousand milliseconds. In real life.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: Fun fact: light from the Moon takes about one point three seconds to reach your eyes. So today, your whole world feels about as far away as the Moon.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: Day three. Four seconds.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: Conversations fall apart. Someone asks you a question. You hear it four seconds later. By the time you answer, they've already walked away.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: Day five. Sixteen seconds.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: And that's when you learn the scariest thing about lag.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: You step off the curb. The street looks empty.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: It was empty. Sixteen seconds ago.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: A horn screams. Something yanks your hoodie back. And sixteen seconds later, you finally see it. A truck. And Mia. Holding onto you with both hands.

lines.speaker: MIA
lines.text: You can't go outside alone anymore. Okay? Promise me.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: Day seven. Sixty-four seconds. More than a full minute.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: Your parents take you to the hospital. The doctors run every test. Eyes: perfect. Ears: perfect. Brain scan: perfect.

lines.speaker: DOC
lines.text: Everything works. It just... arrives late. Like a video that's buffering.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: Then you look in a mirror. And it's empty.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: You stand there. You wait. And a minute later, you walk in. You watch yourself, from one minute ago, walk into the room.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: You're not looking at a mirror anymore. You're watching a recording.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: Day ten. Five hundred and twelve seconds. About eight and a half minutes.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: And here's the strange part. That's almost exactly how long sunlight takes to reach the Earth.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: Whenever anyone looks at the Sun, they see it as it was eight minutes ago. Now you see your entire world that way.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: Someone posts a video of you. The boy who lives eight minutes in the past. Ten million views in one day.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: Scientists want to study you. Strangers want to test you. But you only want one thing. To see the present. Even for one second.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: Day fourteen. Two hours and sixteen minutes.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: You wake up at seven in the morning. And it's pitch black.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: Because your eyes are still living at five a.m.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: Your life splits in two. Your body is in one time. Your world is in another.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: So you learn to live by memory. Twelve steps to the kitchen. Four to the fridge. Mia puts tape on the floor, so you can feel the way.

lines.speaker: MIA
lines.text: Left. Left. Stop. Okay, you're at the table. I'll tell Mom you said thanks.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: Day eighteen. Thirty-six hours. You're living a day and a half in the past.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: And now, you see everything too late to help.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: You watch Mia come home from school, crying, sitting alone on the stairs. You run to her. But the stairs are empty.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: That happened yesterday. She's already fine. She's already asleep.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: You can see everything. You just can't change any of it.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: Day twenty-two. Twenty-four days.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: Your birthday happens. Cake. Candles. Your whole family singing.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: And you won't see any of it for three and a half weeks.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: So on a quiet Tuesday, alone in an empty living room, the party finally reaches you. Balloons appear out of nowhere. Your family sings to an empty chair.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: So you sit down in it. Three weeks late. And you blow out candles that aren't there anymore.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: Day twenty-six. The number on your screen reads thirty-three million seconds. More than a year.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: And then something happens. You walk into your room... and Biscuit is on your bed.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: Biscuit. Your dog. The one you buried last spring.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: He looks up. His tail thumps the blanket. Because to your eyes, it's a year ago. And he's still here.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: You sit next to him for hours. You can't touch him. You don't care.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: And for the first time, you don't want the lag to stop.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: And the next morning... it doesn't move. Day twenty-seven: one year. Day twenty-eight: one year. The doubling has stopped. You're stuck. Exactly one year behind everyone you love.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: That night, your mom finds a box of sticky notes under Mia's bed. Hundreds of them.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: She's been leaving you messages. Not for you now. For the you who will see this room a year from now.

lines.speaker: MIA
lines.text: Hi. It's Mia. Today is day one for me. You'll see this in a year. I'm still here.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: Every single day, she writes one. Because she figured out the one thing the doctors missed.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: Nothing you lose to the lag is ever really lost. Every hug. Every word. Every hand that held yours. It all still reaches you. Just... late.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: And one morning, a year later, you feel it. Small fingers. Squeezing your hand. Right on time.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: Day four hundred. The number on your screen changes color.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: It turns green. And it starts going down.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: Thirty million. Ten million. Ten thousand. Ten. Three. Two. One.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: Zero.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: And then... minus one.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: Now you're seeing one second into the future.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: But that's another story. Would you take the lag... if it meant one more day with someone you lost? Tell me in the comments.
